creator: Alexander Terp
description:
From #153, batch 11, item 1.

`print_err` passes the message to a printf-style function as the format string, so any `%` corrupts the output with no error:

```rad
print_err("a%40nb 100%d")
print("a%40nb 100%d")
```

```
a%!n(MISSING)b 100%!d(MISSING)
a%40nb 100%d
```

URL-encoded ids (`/api/items/foo%40bar`), SQL `LIKE` patterns and percentages all hit it. The reporter routed stderr through `printf '%s'` to work around it.

Confirmed on main (3459ddf1). It is the only `ScriptStderrf` call site; the other `*Stderrf` callers pass fixed formats.

Where: core/func_print.go:43, `RP.ScriptStderrf(resolvePrintStr(f))` should be `ScriptStderrf("%s", ...)`.
title: print_err mangles any message containing %
